s.q: Through the tape-recorder hiss, "Game of Pricks" is like every song on Meet the Beatles rolled into one, and shot out of a cannon into your solar plexus.

s.t: Songfacts reads the song as largely a metaphor for the corporate music industry, which Guided By Voices had entered after about a decade as a little-heard indie band.
s.src: Game Of Pricks by Guided By Voices (Songfacts)
s.q: The "Game Of Pricks" is largely a metaphor for the corporate music industry, which Guided By Voices had entered into after about a decade as a little-heard indie band.

s.t: Robert Pollard says this 1:33 four-track recording has “almost become our signature song. Up there with ‘I Am A Scientist.’”
s.src: A Salty Salute: The Oral History Of Guided By Voices’ ’90s Indie Classic ‘Alien Lanes’ (Uproxx)
s.q: It’s almost become our signature song. Up there with “I Am A Scientist.”

s.t: Alien Lanes was mastered from cassette by Bob Ludwig, who reassured Tobin Sprout he’d done it before, on Springsteen’s Nebraska. Pollard: “I don’t know what the mastering did for it.”
s.src: A Salty Salute: The Oral History Of Guided By Voices’ ’90s Indie Classic ‘Alien Lanes’ (Uproxx)
s.q: “So have you ever done a master from a cassette?” And he said, “Yeah.” Because he did Nebraska by Bruce Springsteen. ... Pollard: With all due respect, I don’t know what the mastering did for it.

f.t: In 14 years as a schoolteacher, Robert Pollard never went to the teachers’ lounge: “I would go off and take a nap to try to get rid of my hangover.”
f.q: I never went to the teachers' lounge. ... But I would go off and take a nap to try to get rid of my hangover. I had 14 years of that.

f.t: Pollard’s fourth-graders in Dayton called him “Mr. Rocker” once they found out about his other job. He quit teaching near “a nervous breakdown, trying to balance both professions.”
f.q: Pollard spent much of his adult life teaching fourth grade in Dayton, Ohio, answering to “Mr. Rocker” after his students found out what his other job was. ... “about ready to have a nervous breakdown, trying to balance both professions.

f.t: To pay for Guided By Voices’ early records, Pollard, his brother and their manager borrowed from the Dayton Public Schools credit union. Pressings ran 300 to 1,000 copies.
f.q: To finance the band's early recordings, Pollard, his brother, and their manager obtained a loan from the Dayton Public Schools credit union. ... the pressings ran only to between 300 and 1,000 copies of each

f.t: Their 1993 show at New York’s New Music Seminar was the band’s first live date in almost six years; Guided By Voices had largely been a basement recording project.
f.q: Guided by Voices got back together in 1993, and played a show that year at the New Music Seminar in New York City – the band's first live date in almost six years.

f.t: Robert Pollard has nearly 3,000 songs registered to his name with BMI, and in 2006 Paste ranked him the 78th-greatest living songwriter.
f.q: He has nearly 3,000 songs registered to his name with BMI. In 2006, Paste magazine listed him as the 78th-greatest living songwriter.
